newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on commercials, hedges.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on commercials, hedges.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down on commercial selling and hedges, traders said.

"Commercial selling came into the market when Chicago weakened. There were MOC (market on close) hedges," a trader said. UGG and Louis Dreyfus bought while Cargill sold, traders said. Sep-Nov spread at $6, Nov Jan $5, Nov May $7. Volume was 5,125 lots, traders said.
September canola rose $3 to $426.80 on commercial demand but November lost $2.90 to $427.40 and January fell $2.80 to $432.90.
October flax up $0.60 to $383.10 on commercials, November up $0.50 to $358.50. Volume was 42 lots.
Cargill sold October peas up US$0.20 at US$210 to LFG.
"There's some concerned short covering in feed grains with early harvest showing good grades but we're getting cool and wet again and nobody seems to care," a trader said.

November western barley rose $1 to $150.30 and February closed up $0.70 to $155.20. October wheat finished up $5 at $206.50 and December was up $4 at $191.50. Oct-Dec spread at $15, Oct-Mar $13.90, Dec-Mar $1. Oats did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
